kurz: How the Riester pension and the basic pension are subsidised, which product suits whom, and why the ongoing reform makes it necessary to review both products again.

bloecke.md:
The Riester pension (Riester-Rente) and the basic pension (Basisrente) are both regarded as state-subsidised, but the support works in completely different ways. Riester pays state allowances (Zulagen), that is, fixed amounts in euros that rise with the number of children and do not depend on income. The basic pension, usually called Rürup after its namesake, provides support through the [[marginal tax rate]]. The contribution reduces taxable income, so the saving grows with the tax rate.

The two routes of support therefore favour opposite groups. Riester mainly benefits savers with children and low incomes, the basic pension mainly childless people with high incomes. Households in between receive no significant support from either product. This relationship explains most of the wrong decisions made with both products.

## Riester subsidies in 2026

The Bundestag passed the Retirement Provision Reform Act (Altersvorsorgereformgesetz) on 27 March 2026, and the Bundesrat did so on 8 May 2026. On 1 January 2027, the new subsidised retirement investment account (Altersvorsorgedepot) starts and replaces new business in Riester contracts. Until then, the previous amounts apply, which have been unchanged since 2018: a basic allowance of €175, a child allowance of €185 for children born before 2008, €300 for younger children and a one-off career starter bonus of €200 for savers who are not yet 25 at the start of the first subsidised contribution year.

The full allowance is only paid if the saver pays in a minimum own contribution (Mindesteigenbeitrag). If less is paid in, the allowance is reduced proportionally. This reduction is the most common and most expensive mistake in handling Riester contracts.

bloecke.formel: Minimum own contribution = min(4% × previous year's gross, €2,100) − allowances, at least €60
bloecke.erklaerung: What counts is the previous year's gross income subject to pension insurance contributions, not that of the current year. The allowances are deducted from the required contribution. They are therefore part of the payment and not an additional bonus.
variablen: Subsidy rate under Section 86 EStG (Income Tax Act); anyone who does not reach 4% receives the allowance only in the same proportion
Maximum amount deductible as special expenses (Sonderausgaben) under Section 10a EStG, including allowances
Base amount that must be paid even without income
bloecke.beispiel: For a single, childless person with €70,000 gross in the previous year, 4% initially gives €2,800, capped at €2,100; less the €175 allowance, this leaves an own contribution of €1,925. With a payment of only €1,200, 62.3% of this is reached, and there is also only 62.3% of the allowance, around €109 instead of €175.

bloecke.md: In addition to the allowances, Riester contributions of up to €2,100 a year can be deducted as special expenses. For this, the tax office automatically carries out the most-favourable assessment (Günstigerprüfung) under Section 10a EStG. If the tax saving is greater than the allowances, the difference is refunded. If it is smaller, the allowances alone apply. The allowances and the tax saving are never both granted in full.

The most-favourable assessment does not change this, because her tax saving of around €275 remains well below the allowances. For the childless high earner, the ratio is reversed. The allowance covers only 8% of his contribution, and the deduction as special expenses a further 28%.

bloecke.md:
- If a Riester contract is terminated and cashed in, all allowances and tax advantages are reclaimed. Making the contract paid-up, by contrast, only costs the future subsidy.
- Without a permanent allowance application (Dauerzulagenantrag), the allowance must be applied for separately every year. Marriage, births, jumps in income and changes of provider must be reported, otherwise the allowance is reduced retroactively.
- If the own contribution is too small, the allowance is reduced proportionally. This is easily overlooked because the reduction does not appear as a loss in the contract statement.

However, the subsidy rate only shows what goes into the contract, not what comes out at the end. At the start of the pension, Riester contracts must guarantee at least the sum of all contributions and allowances. Because of this 100% guarantee, the provider has to invest mainly in low-yielding bonds. On top of this come acquisition and distribution costs, as well as ongoing administration costs and annuitisation based on very cautious mortality tables. Under Section 1(1) sentence 1 no. 8 AltZertG (Pension Contracts Certification Act), the acquisition and distribution costs must be spread evenly over at least the first five years of the contract, unless they are deducted as a percentage of the contributions. For insurance contracts, the maximum Zillmer rate of 2.5% of total contributions under Section 4 DeckRV (Actuarial Reserves Ordinance) only limits the Zillmer adjustment (Zillmerung); the agreed acquisition costs can be higher. The figures for existing contracts show how savers have reacted. At the end of 2025, there were still 14.66 million contracts, 318,000 fewer than a year earlier. Just over a fifth to just under a quarter of them are dormant, meaning that no more contributions are paid into them.

## Retirement investment account from 2027

With the retirement investment account, subsidised retirement capital may for the first time be invested without a guarantee in funds, ETFs and euro bonds of public issuers; individual shares remain excluded. Products with an 80% or 100% capital guarantee remain available. A new addition is a standard product with a capped reduction in yield (Effektivkosten). During the parliamentary process, the cap was lowered from an original 1.5% to 1.0% a year. Existing Riester contracts enjoy grandfathering protection and can switch to the new system without the previous subsidy being reclaimed. The lesson “The retirement investment account” describes the new rules in detail.

bloecke.unter: The allowance rises in two stages and stops growing from an own contribution of €1,800. The subsidy rate falls from 33% for small contributions to 23% at €1,800 and to 7% at the highest permitted contribution of €6,840.

bloecke.md: The Retirement Provision Reform Act of 26 May 2026 has been promulgated (Federal Law Gazette, BGBl. 2026 I No. 156). From 2027, retirement provision contributions of up to €1,800 a year plus the allowances due are deductible as special expenses (Section 10a(1) EStG, new version). For new contracts, the payout begins at the earliest at 65 or with a statutory old-age pension that starts earlier, and at the latest at 70. Up to 30% of the capital can be paid out separately at the start, and a payout plan may not end before the holder reaches the age of 85 (Section 1(1) AltZertG, new version).

## Support and lock-in with the Rürup pension

The basic pension is the counterpart to the Riester pension. It offers no allowances, but in return the largest deduction volume in German tax law. In 2026, up to €30,826 (separate assessment) or €61,652 (joint assessment) is 100% deductible as special expenses. The amount corresponds to the maximum contribution to the miners' pension insurance (knappschaftliche Rentenversicherung), that is, a contribution assessment ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) of €124,800 times 24.7%.

bloecke.formel: Deductible = min(statutory pension and professional pension scheme contributions + basic pension contributions, €30,826) − tax-free employer share
bloecke.erklaerung: The maximum amount applies jointly to all contributions in the first layer. For employees, part of it is therefore already used up, depending on salary, by contributions to the statutory pension insurance before they pay the first euro into a basic pension (Section 10(1) no. 2 and (3) EStG).
bloecke.beispiel: For an employee with €60,000 gross, the 18.6% pension contribution from employer and employee together amounts to €11,160. This leaves €19,666 of headroom. However, the tax-free employer share of €5,580 is then subtracted from the deductible amount again. Self-employed people without statutory pension insurance, by contrast, have the full maximum amount available.

bloecke.md:
A self-employed woman with a taxable income of €80,000 pays €10,000 into a basic pension.

- Income tax without the contribution (Section 32a EStG, 2026 tax scale, rounded down to whole euros): €22,464
- Income tax with the contribution (taxable income €70,000): €18,264
- Saving on income tax: €4,200.00
- Solidarity surcharge without the contribution €251.56, with the contribution €0, because the contribution brings the assessed tax below the exemption threshold (Freigrenze) of €20,350

The total saving is €4,451.56, that is, 44.5% of the contribution. The net cost is €5,548.

The tax saving is only a deferral; the tax falls due later. In the payout phase, the basic pension is subject to the same deferred taxation as the statutory pension. For a pension starting in 2026, 84% of the pension is taxable, and the share rises by 0.5 percentage points for each cohort. The tax-free part is determined as a fixed amount in euros for the year after the pension starts and then applies for life. Regular pension increases are therefore fully taxable.

bloecke.titel: Taxable portion of the basic pension by year in which the pension starts
bloecke.unter: Since the Growth Opportunities Act (Wachstumschancengesetz), the share rises by only 0.5 instead of 1.0 percentage points per cohort. For a pension starting in 2046, 94% is taxable, and today's saving is then repaid at the personal tax rate.

bloecke.md: A basic pension cannot be surrendered, converted into a lump sum, borrowed against or transferred. There is no lump-sum option; only a lifelong life annuity is paid, from 62 at the earliest. A basic pension can only be passed on to heirs through additional modules that cost extra, such as an annuity guarantee period (Rentengarantiezeit) or survivors' cover. Without them, the capital remains with the pool of insured persons on death. The basic pension is therefore unsuitable for savers who need liquidity or want to pass on wealth. On the other hand, the balance in the accumulation phase is protected against seizure and insolvency, which can be an argument in its own right for the self-employed.

## Tax advantage and costs compared

The tax advantage alone is not enough for an assessment. What matters is whether it more than offsets the higher costs compared with a simple securities account. According to market overviews, unit-linked policies have a [[Reduction in yield (Effektivkosten)|reduction in yield]] of around 1.8% to 2.7% a year, and an ETF savings plan including TER usually less than 0.3%. The following comparison assumes the same outlay after tax. A payment of €10,000 into the basic pension costs €5,800 net at a 42% marginal tax rate. Only €5,800 therefore goes into the securities account as well.

bloecke.md: At a 42% marginal tax rate, the basic pension comes out ahead even with an expensive commission-based tariff. The advantage results from the gap between the tax rates. Today 42% is saved; in old age the effective burden is around 27.2% (96.5% of the pension for a pension starting in 2051 at a marginal tax rate of 28.2%). The lower today's tax rate, the smaller this gap and hence the room for costs.

bloecke.md: The benefit of a basic pension depends on the gap between the tax rate today and in retirement, which is not known when the contract is taken out. Above a marginal tax rate of around 40%, it pays off with almost any tariff. Below 30%, it only pays off with a very low-cost net or fee-based tariff, and below 25% practically never.

Employees with middle incomes, whose marginal tax rate is usually too low to offset the usual policy costs

Offers with a reduction in yield above 2% at a marginal tax rate below 40%

bloecke.md: If you are likely to receive basic income support in old age (Grundsicherung im Alter), the assessment is reversed. Lifelong pensions from additional retirement provision, that is, from Riester, Rürup and company pension contracts, but also from private pension insurance, are not counted as income up to €281.50 a month in 2026 (Section 82(4) and (5) SGB XII, the Social Code Book on social assistance). The first €100 is exempt in full, plus 30% of the amount above it, up to a total of half of standard needs level 1 (Regelbedarfsstufe 1). Freely available portfolio assets, by contrast, are counted as assets. With a foreseeably small pension, a subsidised contract is therefore more favourable here than a securities account. This difference is rarely mentioned, but it is considerable.

- Do not terminate existing Riester contracts. Making them paid-up or switching to the new system, which from 2027 does not jeopardise the subsidy, is almost always better.
- Before taking out any contract, compare the reduction in yield in the product information sheet (Produktinformationsblatt), not just the fund costs, because the TER is only part of the costs.
- For pension products, ask about the guaranteed [[Annuity conversion factor (Rentenfaktor)|annuity conversion factor (Rentenfaktor)]], not the projected one, because only the guaranteed one is in the contract.
- Work out your own marginal tax rate before considering a basic pension. Below 35%, searching for a suitable tariff is rarely worthwhile.
- Submit a permanent allowance application and report changes regarding children, income and marital status.

mitnehmen: Riester provides support through allowances that depend on the number of children, Rürup through the deduction as special expenses, which grows with the marginal tax rate; households in between hardly benefit from either.

In the examples, the Riester subsidy rate from allowances and tax advantage ranges from around 28% for the childless household with a middle income to over 69% for single parents with two younger children.

New Riester business ends on 31 December 2026; from 2027 there is the retirement investment account without a mandatory guarantee, with a basic allowance of up to €540 and a cost cap of 1.0% for the standard product.
The tax advantage of the Rürup pension is a deferral, because for a pension starting in 2046, 94% of the pension is taxable.

Whether a basic pension yields more than a securities account depends solely on the relationship between the tax rate gap and the reduction in yield; at a 42% marginal tax rate it may cost 2.72%, at 25% only 0.82%.

begriffe.text: Amount that a Riester saver must pay in personally to receive the full allowance. It is 4% of the previous year's gross income subject to pension insurance contributions, at most €2,100, less the allowances, but at least €60. If it is not reached, the allowance falls in the same proportion.

Automatic comparison by the tax office under Section 10a EStG between the allowances received and the tax saving from the deduction as special expenses. Only the more favourable option is granted; if the tax saving exceeds the allowances, the difference is refunded.

Lifelong life annuity in the first layer of retirement provision, usually called the Rürup pension after its namesake. Contributions of up to €30,826 (2026) are fully deductible as special expenses, and the pension is subject to deferred taxation. Surrender, a lump-sum option and borrowing against the contract are excluded.

The successor product to the Riester pension, eligible for subsidies from 1 January 2027. For the first time, it may invest in funds and ETFs without a capital guarantee; it is subsidised with a basic allowance of up to €540 plus €300 per child.

Statutory key figure for retirement provision products (Section 7 AltZertG in conjunction with Section 8 no. 3 AltvPIBV, the Retirement Provision Product Information Sheet Ordinance, and for life insurance Section 2(1) no. 9 VVG-InfoV, the Insurance Information Obligations Ordinance), known in German as Effektivkosten. It states by how many percentage points all costs together reduce the gross return per year, and it is the only meaningful yardstick for comparing policies with securities account solutions.
